name: Should I remodel my pool before selling my house in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: Should I remodel my pool before selling my house in Los Angeles?
mainEntity.text: Should I remodel my pool before selling my house in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: A pool remodel before selling makes the most sense when the pool is a visible negative during showings. Cracked coping, stained plaster, broken tile, or aging equipment can make a home feel neglected and can scare buyers away. In many Los Angeles neighborhoods, a clean and functional pool is a strong selling feature, but a full luxury remodel rarely returns every dollar spent. The best pre-sale projects are usually the ones that improve first impressions and reduce buyer objections: resurfacing, fixing leaks, repairing tile and coping, refreshing lighting, and making the equipment look reliable and well maintained. Large custom upgrades, like major reshaping or high-end water features, may not be worth the cost if the sale is near-term. Sellers should focus on condition, not just style. A contractor can help identify whether the pool needs only cosmetic updates or whether hidden issues could become inspection problems. If the pool is old but functional, a targeted remodel may be more effective than a full redesign.
acceptedAnswer.description: A pool remodel before selling can help when the pool looks dated, damaged, or expensive to maintain, but not every upgrade pays back equally. Cosmetic fixes, leak repair, and visible surface improvements usually matter more than luxury add-ons. The right choice depends on neighborhood expectations, home price, and how buyers use outdoor space.
